contentText: In a week where assassinations have continued within the top ranks of Iran’s regime, the minister of intelligence, the commander of the Bases paramilitary and the powerful security chief Ali Larijani included, but a weakened government seems to have had little bearing on Tehran’s retaliation across Israel and nine gulf states.Just one week ago, President Trump spoke of a war that was,  “very complete, pretty much”, that now appears to have been premature, and over-confident. There’s no more talk of a Venezuelanstyle regime change that works for Washington. And Israel’s actual cooperation with Washington has come under scrutiny, after Israeli air strikes on the world’s largest natural gas field, at South Pars, which provides power for an estimated 70 to 80% of Iranians. President Trump’s immediate response was that he knew nothing about it. Insiders questioned the remark, critics claimed it spoke of the US getting sucked further into an Israeli agenda. Israel’s prime minister said that was nonsens.
